adds.title: Novaya Gazeta - April 2017 investigation
adds.summary: In late March 2017 authorities in Chechnya detained over 100 men across Grozny and other settlements for actual or suspected non-traditional sexual orientation, including muftiate religious figures and television presenters who had concealed their orientation, with at least three detainees killed and further killings alleged, while those released fled the republic and users abandoned LGBT messenger groups and closed social-media accounts because non-traditional orientation carries lethal honor-based retaliation risk amid close social monitoring.

adds.title: Supreme Court of Russia - November 2023 ruling designating 'international LGBT public movement' as extremist
adds.summary: On 30 November 2023 Russia's Supreme Court designated the 'international LGBT public movement' as extremist and outlawed it, banning LGBT including trans organization, advocacy and symbols nationwide including in Dagestan and exposing trans visitors to administrative and criminal liability for public expression, display, or advocacy.
